A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SARD study. The main text, algorithm, equations, figures, nine tables and Appendices A–E can be matched and inspected despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: Sections 6.1–6.3 and Appendix E report original classification, regression and object-detection experiments comparing SARD with existing deferral methods under clean and adversarial conditions.

after.justification: Sections 6.1–6.3 and Appendix E retain these original experiments, including accuracy, RMSE and mAP results with uncertainty reporting.

M1.justification: The targeted and untargeted attack objectives, cost-weighted surrogates, regularized SARD objective and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures. Expanded explanations and the computational analysis do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100 classification, California Housing regression and Pascal VOC object detection with the same expert populations and attack scenarios. The new medical inference schematic is illustrative, not an additional evaluation.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Mao et al. (2023a), Regression with multi-expert deferral, and Montreuil et al. (2024). The regression reference changes from Mao et al. (2024d) to (2024c), but its identity and comparison participation are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 6 and Appendix E retain the same splits, architectures, metrics, training budgets, hyperparameters and PGD settings, including 40/10/20 steps for classification/regression/multi-task learning. Section 5.3 adds computational analysis without revising the reported experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The weak-expert and agent-targeted robustness evaluations, including primary-model targets in Appendix E, are retained. No ablation, sensitivity study, error analysis or empirical case study is added; Appendix B redraws conceptual illustrations.

E5.justification: Appendix E specifies means and standard deviations over four independent trials in both versions. The uncertainty reporting practices and reported uncertainty values are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in corresponding Tables 1–9 are identical, including the additional model-targeted results in Appendix E. The reported rankings, attack effects and clean-versus-adversarial performance findings are also retained.

T1.justification: New Section 5.3 adds Proposition 5.13 and its proof concerning epoch cost and peak memory. Section 5.2 adds analysis of the applicability of Wang and Scott's calibration conditions. The central consistency bounds and Appendix D proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same scientific scope: two routing attacks, convex SARD with Bayes- and (R,G)-consistency guarantees, and robustness across three task types. Revised emphasis on efficiency and clean performance does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly explains why nondifferentiability prevents direct application of Wang and Scott's calibration theorem. Section 5.3 discusses training bottlenecks and robustness-versus-computation tradeoffs through expert count and PGD depth. Existing experimental interpretations and the rejector-only threat scope are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 newly documents forward/backward-pass accounting and activation storage during sequential PGD processing. Appendix E retains the same implementation settings, NVIDIA H100 hardware disclosure and statement about publicly available scripts.

R1.justification: v2 adds selective-prediction context, Narasimhan et al. (2022) on post-hoc deferral, Strong et al. (2024) on healthcare, and Wang and Scott (2023) on calibration. It removes the citation to Principled approaches for learning to defer with multiple experts. These refine positioning without changing the central research relationship.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, L2D related-work discussion and substantial explanatory passages in Sections 3–5 are rewritten. Existing inline definitions become numbered statements, and complexity, acknowledgment and impact sections are added. The editorial revision extends well beyond isolated copyediting.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML layout with two-column main text and wider single-column appendices. Both attack diagrams are substantially redrawn and grouped with a new inference diagram in Appendix B. Tables and long proof displays are resized, repositioned and reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves accessibility through clearer routing diagrams, more explicit definitions and better contextualization against prior research, while preserving the experimental evidence. The new complexity discussion adds useful context, although Proposition 5.13 leaves sample-versus-batch accounting unclear and the modest-overhead assertion lacks timing measurements. The net gain is mainly explanatory, rather than a substantial strengthening of the scientific evidence.
